alignments.note: Attributive demonstrative takes the English determiner slot.
Rule 38: the demonstrative already occupies the determiner slot, so the article realizes nothing.
Genitive-absolute participle rendered as a finite clause; the supplied subordinator *when* and expletive subject are rule 7/86 helpers on the participle, which licenses the subordination.
Rule 58: adjective and noun both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner *a* belongs to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15.

Rule 59: the negator stands with a plain indefinite carrying no negation of its own, so the single English word spells the negation into *no-* and the indefinite into *-thing* and the pair is one unit. Giving *nothing* to the indefinite alone and emptying the negator under rule 41 is the competing reading, but rule 41 requires a second negative word.
Participle rendered as a finite clause with supplied subject.
Subjunctive rendered by the infinitive; *to* is its own rule 7 helper, no conjunction governing the clause.
προσκαλέομαι is *call unto him(self)*; the reflexive complement is part of the verb's own English expression.
Rule 20 second arm: no genitive pronoun stands to take the supplied possessive, so the article is what *his* realizes.
Rule 88: the participle is converted to a coordinate finite clause and the supplied juncture *and* is a helper on the finite verb it introduces.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition.

review_notes: The μή/τί pair is joined under rule 59's plain-indefinite arm; rule 41 would empty μή only if the second word were itself a negative.
Both supplied possessives and junctures are rule 7 helpers, not `added`.
